title: Forensic Facial Specialists Can Identify People Using Just a Couple Facial Features - Nautilus
gist: Facial recognition AI is about 99 percent accurate in lab conditions but degrades with bad lighting, sunglasses or clothing; understanding human forensic facial specialists could help train the machines.

insights.claim: AI facial recognition correctly identifies people 99 percent of the time in lab conditions, but real-world factors such as poor lighting, sunglasses and clothing can cause failures or false positives.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Lab accuracy overstates field performance; discount vendor claims for deployments in uncontrolled settings.
insights.locator: In lab conditions, it's extraordinarily precise

insights.claim: Better understanding of how human forensic facial specialists identify people could help train AI facial recognition systems.
insights.speaker: Jake Currie
insights.so_what: Human-expert benchmarking may be a path to more robust biometric models.
insights.locator: Of course, we already have human forensic facial specialists
